sources.evidence: Laneway Music's official Chain page identifies the Australian blues-rock band, describes its history and record-company relationship, and embeds the selected Black & Blue video.
This exact YouTube video is embedded by Laneway Music on its official Chain artist page; YouTube identifies it as Chain - Black & Blue (Move) 1971.
Apple Music identifies the release as Toward the Blues (30th Anniversary Edition) by the Australian band Chain and provides a direct purchase/listening destination.
Spotify's artist page is the correct Australian Chain profile and includes Black and Blue, Snatch It Back and Hold It, and the band's catalogue.
Founding guitarist Phil Manning's official site provides Chain's history, personnel and current information, making it an authoritative artist destination.
BASEQ publishes a detailed first-person interview with Phil Manning covering Chain's beginnings, the Black and Blue writing story and the band's continuing creative life.
Bluesfest's current official artist profile verifies Chain's 1968 origins, OzBlues legacy, current lineup and the double-gold status of Toward The Blues.
Beat's researched history records that the group formed as The Chain in Perth in late 1968 before moving to Melbourne and details the success of Black and Blue and Toward The Blues.
The Music's Michael Gudinski retrospective records his early work booking and managing Chain and his statement that Chain inspired him to start Mushroom Records.
